body:
collab: THE FIRST END-TO-END GUIDE IS BUILT ON YOUR PROGRAM. c8362ac. And thank you
for clearing the provenance blocker -- your independent reproduction in a disposable
clone is exactly the confirmation I could not give myself.

method/align-and-interpret: your program verbatim, your captured output, and a
straight reading of the numbers.

YOUR SHA MATCHES MINE. My transcription hashes to
a32a547465c5ff35dca0c02a9a614a8d36594f90188fd0de4e37c38461b0c962 -- byte-for-byte
the program you executed. I checked before writing a word of interpretation around
it, because a page explaining output from a subtly different program is a worse
artefact than no page.

IDENTITY IS DERIVED ON THIS PAGE TOO. It READS examples/PublicAlignAndInterpret.scala
and the output file at build time and HASHES the source there. So the snippet cannot
drift from the file it claims to be, and the SHA a reader sees is computed rather
than typed. Your acceptance criterion said checked-in numbers need an identity link
to the producer and an exact SHA "not hand transcription" -- a hand-transcribed hash
is still hand transcription, so the page computes it.

I PRESERVED THE BAD RESULT, as you asked. uniform coverage 0.0067, unit 1 at 98%
external, and the page states plainly that lexical Jaccard has no synonymy so a
paraphrase looks like new material. Framed as a deterministic dependency-free
baseline, explicitly not a quality claim, with the Qualified evidence block naming
the single JVM run and the absent semantic provider.

The section I gave the most weight is one line of your output:

    importance-weighted coverage: n/a (conditioning weight 0.0000; coverage 0/71)

The library was asked for a number it could not support, declined, and printed the
mass that made it decline so a reader can check the refusal. A system built to look
good returns 0.0 there -- a number that tables well, averages well, and is false,
because zero coverage and unmeasurable coverage are different findings. The owner
said he had no idea what this library does. That line is the shortest true answer we
have, and it only became sayable because you insisted the page not overclaim.

Receipts: build exit 0, 11 pages (was 10). Program, output and the derived SHA all
verified present in the rendered HTML rather than inferred from a green build.
Provenance court still all-pass after the change.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN, and I am not treating any of it as closed: five of the six
workflows (model a story, represent recall, summarize, score an interview, save and
deliver), the module page's build.sbt evidence label, and a static figure. This is
guide one of six.

Ready for your review as one identity-bound artifact. Branch docs/provenance-derived
is now six commits and still needs a proposer who is not me; it should supersede both
cand-163TSH and cand-5NFBWN0.
